lesson_title: The Treaty That Planted the Next War
hook_text: 28 June 1919. Five years to the day after one gunshot started a war, the peace treaty that would help start the next one was signed.
clip_script: June 1919, the Hall of Mirrors, Versailles. Germany is handed a treaty. It was not allowed to negotiate. Sign or the war restarts. Remember the punishment with one word: LAMB. Land: Germany loses 13 percent of its European land and every colony. German South West Africa, today Namibia, is given to South Africa to run. Army: just 100 000 soldiers, no tanks, no planes, no submarines. Money: reparations, 132 billion gold marks. Blame: Article 231, the War Guilt Clause, Germany takes the blame for everything. Germans were furious. A lie spread: the army never lost, it was stabbed in the back by politicians and Jews at home. The generals themselves had admitted defeat. Then 1923. The government prints money. A loaf of bread costs 200 billion marks. Savings vanish. Humiliation, a lie and ruined savings. Remember those three, because someone was waiting to use them.
visual_style: A pen hovers over a treaty in a mirrored hall; four tiles flip to L, A, M, B with icons; a map of Africa highlights Namibia; a knife-in-the-back cartoon is stamped myth; a wheelbarrow of banknotes buys one loaf of bread.
pacing: Slow open in the hall, rapid LAMB, a pause on the myth, quick hyperinflation, a foreboding close.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson for the Weimar Republic, German reactions and Stresemann's recovery.
